Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

Bots inside your agent IDE.

Open source. Bring your own everything: your Claude Code or Codex, your local or remote machines, your tools. Ask from Slack or your phone. When it needs you, it's one tab away.

Download Orca  ·  Explore bots →

## Features
### Orca Bots Ask a bot in Slack, Linear, or GitHub to fix a bug, and come back to a tested pull request. It runs on your own Claude Code or Codex. Open its work in Orca to review it or step in. [Overview](https://orca.dev/bots) · [Security](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/bots)
### Chat or Terminal Run any agent in Chat UI or as the raw CLI, and move a conversation between the two without losing context. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/native-chat)
### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)
### Mobile App Pair Orca with the mobile app to get pinged when an agent needs you, reply in chat, and keep work moving on any of your machines when you are away from your desk. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Android APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Review AI Output Review diffs, leave notes on exact changed lines, and send focused feedback back to an agent. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Git Integration Draft commit messages and pull requests from the diff, then send failing checks or PR review comments back to an agent to fix. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/commit-push)
### Parallel Worktrees Quickly split tasks into isolated environments, so multiple agents can work side by side without interfering with each other. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Design Mode Click any element in Orca's browser to copy its HTML, styles, and selector, then paste it into your agent's chat. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native See your GitHub and Linear tasks in one place, and start a workspace for each when you're ready to build. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### Orca CLI Anything you can do in Orca, your agents can do too: create worktrees, start workers, drive the browser and desktop apps, and schedule automations, all from the command line. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
### Plugins Themes, editors, languages, and panels from the community, installed in a click. [Browse plugins →](https://orca.dev/plugins)
### Split Anything Put agents, terminals, browsers, and diffs side by side in split panes shaped to the task. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/tabs-panes-splits)
**Also in the box:** - **[Bot Schedules & Triggers](https://orca.dev/docs/bots#put-it-on-a-schedule)**: run a bot every weekday at 9, or when a pull request opens, a check fails, or a webhook fires. - **[Bot Memory in Markdown](https://orca.dev/docs/bots/security#what-you-can-review)**: a bot's soul and memory are plain Markdown files (`SOUL.md`, `MEMORY.md`) you can read and edit. - **[Drag Files to Agents](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)**: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt. - **[Jump Anywhere](https://orca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)**: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host. - **[Rich Previews](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/viewers)**: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them. - **[Mobile Emulator](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview#mobile-emulator)**: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work. - **[Dictation](https://orca.dev/docs/settings#voice)**: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal. - **[Usage & Accounts](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)**: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out. - **[Automations](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/automations)**: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps. - **[Computer Use](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)**: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers. - **And many, many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

--- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux - **[Download from orca.dev](https://orca.dev/download)** - Or grab a build directly: [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-arm64.dmg) · [macOS Intel](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-x64.dmg) · [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-windows-setup.exe) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-linux.AppImage) · [All builds](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest) _Or via a package manager:_ ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) # Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask. brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Upgrade an existing install brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Release candidates (conflicts with the stable cask; uninstall it first) brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca@rc # Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source yay -S stably-orca-bin ``` ### Mobile App — iOS, Android Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone. - **iOS:** [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) - **Android:** [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=dev.orca.app) · [Download APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Install guide](https://orca.dev/docs/android-apk) --- ## Community & Support - **Discord:** Join the community on **[Discord](https://discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q)**. - **Twitter / X:** Follow **[@orca_build](https://x.com/orca_build)** for updates and announcements. - **WeChat:** Scan to join an Orca community WeChat group. - **Feedback & Ideas:** We ship fast. Missing something? [Request a new feature](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues). - **Privacy:** See the [privacy & telemetry docs](https://orca.dev/docs/telemetry) for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out. - **Show Support:** [Star](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) this repo to follow along with our daily ships. --- ## Developing Want to contribute or run locally? See our [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.

## Signed Builds Windows code signing sponsored/provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). ## License Orca is free and open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

# Introducing OpenGame OpenGame is **the first open-source Super Game Agent** — turning **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, or any of your local coding agents into an AI Unreal Engine / Unity and full-stack game studio. Go from a single idea to **AAA-grade 3D worlds** or **monetization-ready viral mini-games** in one end-to-end pipeline. - 🚀 **Build AAA-Grade 3D Games with Your Agent.** Drive full-stack 3D gameplay, art, music, and voice straight from **DeepSeek (DSH)**, **Claude**, **Codex**, or **Gemini** — from one prompt to playable 3D action, racing, and open-world games. - 🎮 **One-Click Remix & Re-style Any Game.** Start from **25 built-in playable templates** (3D, voxel, anime, pixel & 9:16 hits) with full editable source — keep proven mechanics while swapping characters, worlds, and art styles in minutes. - 💰 **Build Games That Earn: Create → Verify → Monetize.** Automated logic checks, balance simulation, headless playtesting, covers, and gameplay trailers — ship live web links, export single-file **9:16 Playable Ads**, and connect publishing paths for **WeChat Mini Games**, **TikTok**, and **Douyin**. - 🔓 **Full-Stack Open Source (BYOA + BYOK).** Code, art, video, music, voice, SFX, and Three.js 3D are all open source — plug in your favorite [local agent](#agent-wall) and own API keys, or connect [OpenDesign Go](https://go.open-design.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=opengame&utm_content=readme_en) (Black Friday lowest-ever discount, with free access to **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**, **Seedream**, and more). ## ⚡ Quick Start ### 1. Give one prompt to your local Agent Paste this instruction into **DeepSeek TUI / Harness**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **WorkBuddy**, **Cursor**, **Gemini CLI**, or any of the [22 supported local agents](#agent-wall): ```text Follow https://github.com/nexu-io/opengame/blob/main/docs/opengame-setup.md to connect OpenGame to this agent and open the Game Studio template gallery. ``` ### 2. Install the Main OpenGame Skill with Skills CLI Install the main `opengame` entry Skill (which guides local setup and routes into `openmotion-game` + 18 game craft, 3C, animation, playable-ad, and QA reference handbooks) with the [Skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills): ```sh npx skills add https://github.com/nexu-io/opengame/tree/skills --skill opengame ``` > Installing the Skill copies the OpenGame entry instructions into your agent (you can also install `--skill openmotion-game` directly). Complete the local Studio & MCP setup below so your agent can call the 12 `openmotion_game_*` tools and open Game Studio. ### 3. Run OpenGame Studio locally from source Requires **Git**, **Git LFS**, **npm**, and **Node.js 22.18+** (CI pins Node.js 26.11.1). Browse the catalog immediately after startup. Playing or remixing a template downloads its assets on first use. Tidebreaker works offline. ```sh git -c filter.lfs.process= -c filter.lfs.smudge= -c filter.lfs.required=false clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch main https://github.com/nexu-io/opengame.git cd opengame git lfs install --local --skip-smudge npm ci npm run build:studio npm start ``` **Works with 22 local agents (BYOA)** · [Choose your agent](#choose-agent)

## ✨ Why OpenGame ### 1. One-Click Remix & Re-style — Powered by Game-as-Code Building a polished game from a blank prompt is hard for any model. OpenGame solves this by separating **verified game engineering** from **theme, art direction, and content**: - **Every game is clean, inspectable source**: `index.html`, deterministic `logic.js`, vendored Three.js for 3D titles, plus structured design docs (`design/plan.md`, `design/style.md`, `design/assets.csv`, `design/verification.md`). - **Remix in one click**: Click **Remix** on any of the 25 templates in Game Studio (or ask your agent to remix it) to fork an owned, editable draft with full controls, tuning knobs, and automated test hooks already wired up. - **Re-style into any universe**: Swap genre dressing, characters, palette, sprites, textures, and music without breaking physics or win/loss rules — ideal for fast iteration with affordable models like **DeepSeek**, or pushing AAA-grade 3D & shader ambition with **Claude Fable 5.2**, **Opus**, **Codex**, and **Gemini**. **Try these prompts in your connected Agent:** ```text # 1. One-click Remix & Re-style (great for DeepSeek / fast models) Use openmotion-game to remix the "Lantern Hop" template into a cyberpunk rain-city cat runner. Keep the double-jump physics and endless scoring loop, replace the fox and lanterns with a neon cyber-cat and holo-batteries, generate new key art and synthwave BGM, then validate, playtest, and capture a fresh cover. ``` ```text # 2. Build a 9:16 Playable Ad ready for mobile campaigns Use openmotion-game to create a portrait 9:16 playable ad (playableAd: true) for a medieval tower-defense mobile game: instant first-frame interaction with a hand tutorial, a 25-second escalating wave battle, and an end card with an App Store / Google Play CTA. Validate, simulate, playtest at 390x844, and bundle as a single-file HTML. ``` ```text # 3. Original 3D Game from Scratch (great for Claude Fable 5.2 / Opus / Codex / Gemini) Use openmotion-game to create a 3D wuxia boss-duel game (style: "3d") set on a misty bamboo cliff at dusk. Include parry timing, dodge i-frames, stamina management, and two boss phases. Run 3-tier simulation, headless Chromium playtest, capture a 1280x720 cover, and record a gameplay trailer. ``` ### 2. Full-Stack Multimodal Game Creation (BYOK) A real game needs more than code — it needs key art, character sprites, seamless 3D textures, music loops, voice lines, and crisp sound effects. OpenGame's **Model Gateway** wires multimodal generation directly into the game project while keeping your API keys local and separate from game source.


| Game Asset Layer | Recommended Models (when configured in Model Gateway) | Zero-Key / Built-in Fallback | | --- | --- | --- | | **🖼️ Key art, portraits, sprites & textures** | `GPT Image 2.6` (edits & transparent PNGs), `Seedream 5.5` / `5.0 Flash`, `Nano Banana 2`, `FLUX`, `Codex Image` | Crisp procedural Canvas/SVG sprites & procedural textures | | **🎵 Background music (menu, stage, boss)** | `ElevenLabs Music v2` (`no vocals` loops), `Suno v4` | Procedural Web Audio synthesized soundtrack | | **🎙️ Character voice & announcer lines** | `ElevenLabs v3` (English & multilingual), `BytePlus TTS 2` (Chinese), `Kokoro` | Styled dialogue captions & subtitle UI | | **🎬 Intro cutscenes & motion clips** | `Wan 2.7`, `Seedance 2.5` (short I2V clips) | In-engine animated intro camera & title sequence | | **🔊 Impact SFX (hits, jumps, coins, UI)** | Synthesized directly in game code via the Web Audio API | Same (zero latency, zero external files) | | **🧊 3D scenes & models** | Vendored **Three.js** + bundled CC0 kits + reserved 3D gateway slot (auto-discovered when connected) | Procedural Three.js geometry, lighting & shaders | > OpenGame charges no software subscription for the local open-source stack. Use your own provider keys in **Model Settings**, connect [OpenDesign Go](https://go.open-design.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=opengame&utm_content=readme_en) for unified multi-model access, or build 100% code-generated zero-API-cost games. [Model catalog](gateway/catalog.ts) · [Provider setup](docs/model-gateway.md) ### 3. Automated Game QA, Balance Simulation & Auto-Trailers Agents shouldn't just output code and hope it runs. OpenGame enforces an automated engineering verification loop before marking any game **ready**: 1. **Static & 50-Tick Logic Validation (`openmotion_game_validate`)** — Verifies `index.html`, allowed asset/CDN policies, required deterministic exports, and runs a 50-tick smoke test (`< 5 ms` per tick). 2. **3-Tier Deterministic Balance Simulation (`openmotion_game_simulate`)** — Executes bounded headless routes without a browser to verify that a skilled `reference` route reaches a real win milestone, a degraded weak route struggles, and an `idle` player loses cleanly (`< 2500` ticks). 3. **Headless Chromium Playtesting (`openmotion_game_playtest`)** — Drives real keyboard/mouse/touch controls across 1–4 clients, checking 3C responsiveness, `390×844` mobile layout integrity, media URL loads, and zero console/network errors. 4. **Game-Only Cover Capture (`openmotion_game_capture_cover`)** — Captures a clean `1280×720` PNG directly from the game canvas in isolated headless Chrome. 5. **Automated Gameplay Trailer (`openmotion_game_trailer`)** — Records three real 5-second headless gameplay clips at `1280×720`, composes an editable ~19-second title + highlights + Play Now trailer, and renders an MP4 ready for social launch. ## 🚀 End-to-End Distribution & Monetization Turn playable prototypes into real games people can play, share, and pay for. | Stage | Available Today | Roadmap (In Progress) | | --- | --- | --- | | **Play & Local Catalog** | Publish straight to your local OpenGame Studio market (`openmotion_game_publish`) with play tracking, favorites, and 1-click Remix | **Top 100 Profitable Mini-Game Templates** curated by genre & revenue mechanics for instant remixing | | **Instant Web Share** | One-click static bundle & live web share link via OpenDesign Cloud (`openmotion_assets_use action="web_publish"`), rewriting local media URLs and compressing assets automatically | Custom domain & embeddable game widget cards | | **Mobile Playable Ads** | Built-in **9:16 Playable Ad mode** (`playableAd: true`): first-frame instant play, hand tutorial, rich short-level progression, looping BGM, and App Store / Google Play end-card CTA | Direct ad-network packaging presets (AppLovin, Unity Ads, Meta, TikTok) | | **Mini-Game Platforms & Monetization** | Clean self-contained HTML5/JS project exports ready for manual platform wrapping, plus auto-recorded gameplay trailers for launch marketing | **L1–L4 Guided Platform Publishing** (packaging scripts, checklists & Skills) for **WeChat Mini Games (微信小游戏)**, **Douyin Mini Games (抖音小游戏)**, **TikTok**, **Xiaohongshu Mini-Tools**, and **itch.io / Poki / CrazyGames** | | **AI Game Playground** | Local single-player & existing room-based playtesting | **Multi-Model Live Game Arena** — pit multiple frontier LLMs against each other inside live games in real time | ## 🛠️ Setup & MCP Tools ### Connect Your Local Agent Choose your agent to connect the local OpenGame MCP server and Skills:

- **DeepSeek TUI / Harness** · Install the `openmotion-game` skill and connect the local MCP tools via Cordis configuration, or run `node integrations/dsh/install.ts` from the checkout. items.readme_text:
![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **85 skills** · 16 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY

      

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 85 skills + 16 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 85 skills + 16 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install claude-bughunter` (or `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` for the tip of main) — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **85 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 7 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 5 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **16 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — `triage-validation`'s 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The `bugcrowd-reporting` skill includes researcher-side hygiene (Bugcrowdninja alias, account-state restoration, friendly-tester posture) that signals legitimate authorized testing to the target's fraud team. The bundle explicitly **excludes**: weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) for the full posture. > **Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards.** Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that **block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default** — so even *authorized, in-scope* work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's **free, application-based [Cyber Verification Program (CVP)](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case)** to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are *not* adjustable.) Details: [Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604842-real-time-cyber-safeguards-on-claude). ### Why your model switched mid-session Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On **Opus 5**, a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names *exploit generation*, *binary-based vulnerability scanning* and *penetration testing* — **fall back to Opus 4.8** rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See [why Claude switched models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16049681-why-claude-switched-models-in-your-conversation-with-opus-5). What to do depends on what you are actually doing: | Situation | What helps | |---|---| | **Auditing your own code** — reviewing a repo you own for defects | Say so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive. | | **Authorized offensive work** — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submission | This is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is [CVP](https://claude.com/form/cyber-use-case). Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead. | | **You just want the switching off** | Settings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching. | `/hunt` states the engagement frame (authorized, scope-bounded, remediable finding) on its first turn for exactly this reason — engagement context belongs in the session explicitly, not implied. --- ## Documentation | Doc | Contents | |---|---| | [`README.md`](README.md) | This file — overview, quickstart, scope, skill summary | | [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md) | Full setup with Burp MCP integration and optional skill regenerator | | [`USAGE.md`](USAGE.md) | Workflow walkthrough · decision tree · worked engagement example | | [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | 6-phase architecture · skill-to-phase mapping · engagement composition | | [`docs/cbh-cli.md`](docs/cbh-cli.md) | `cbh` CLI — native runner orchestrating recon + classify + triage + report | | [`docs/cve-coverage.md`](docs/cve-coverage.md) | CISA KEV coverage snapshot — refreshed weekly via the workflow template at `docs/automation/cve-refresh.yml.template` | | [`docs/credits.md`](docs/credits.md) | Full attribution: 43 original skills + 8 vendored from upstream | | [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) | PR guidelines · skill quality standards · scope | | [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) | Authorized-use posture · responsible disclosure · what's excluded | | [`LICENSE`](LICENSE) | MIT | | [`NOTICE`](NOTICE) | Upstream-skills attribution · no-redistribution note | | [`LICENSE-CONTENT`](LICENSE-CONTENT) | CC BY 4.0 (skill methodology, wordlists, docs) | --- ## Why this exists Most bug-hunting Claude setups are either too generic (one big "security" prompt) or too fragmented (you bookmark 30 disclosed reports and re-read them every engagement). Neither scales past the second target. This bundle was built and validated through authorized engagements that exposed different capability gaps: **Bug-bounty engagement** — surfaced four gaps a starter 3-skill stack could not close: 1. **No hypothesis discipline** — drafts written before validation → wasted hours, hurt validity ratio 2. **No per-program reporting tactics** — VRT defaults auto-downgraded P3-worthy findings to P4 3. **No engagement coordination** — findings, evidence, and submission IDs scattered across folders 4. **No evidence hygiene** — screenshots leaked cookies and victim PII **External red-team engagement** — exposed five additional gaps that bug-bounty defaults made worse: 1. **Conservative defaults retracted real findings** — WAPT mindset stopped tests early on defended targets where red-team continuation would have surfaced bypass chains → `redteam-mindset` 2. **No mid-engagement situational awareness** — client SOC patched confirmed SQLi within 30 min; external attacker locked 14 accounts during a live test session — both invisible without explicit detection methodology → `mid-engagement-ir-detection` 3. **No enterprise-platform attack chains** — M365 + Entra ID, on-prem SharePoint, Cisco SSL VPN, vCenter, and 7 Android APKs all needed current 2024-2026 CVE knowledge and platform-specific tradecraft → `m365-entra-attack`, `okta-attack`, `hunt-sharepoint`, `hunt-aspnet`, `hunt-ntlm-info`, `vmware-vcenter-attack`, `enterprise-vpn-attack`, `apk-redteam-pipeline` 4. **No client-facing deliverable format** — bug-bounty report templates don't fit enterprise red-team where output is a 50KB+ MD + DOCX with embedded screenshots → `redteam-report-template` 5. **No post-credential escalation model** — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate → `cloud-iam-deep` The per-class `hunt-*` skills address gap-zero (*"what should I look for in webapps"*) — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. The enterprise-platform and red-team-tradecraft layers address what bug-bounty alone cannot: external red-team engagements against monitored enterprise targets. --- ## Roadmap - [x] HackerOne MCP integration — [`mcp/hackerone/`](mcp/hackerone/README.md): disclosed-report duplicate search, program stats and scope; optional logged-in mode for private programs and your own reports - [ ] Per-engagement memory layer — pattern recall across targets - [x] Industry-specific hunt skills — `hunt-fintech-graphql` shipped; `hunt-healthcare-fhir`, `hunt-gov-compliance` still open - [x] Program-scope importer — `cbh scope import` builds `scope.md` from a program's published scope (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack via [bounty-targets-data](https://github.com/arkadiyt/bounty-targets-data); HackerOne MCP output for private programs; or pasted program text), failing closed on anything ambiguous — see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) - [ ] Refresh `hunt-*` skills with newer disclosed reports (re-run `public-skills-builder`) - [ ] Additional enterprise-platform skills — `citrix-netscaler-deep`, `f5-bigip-attack`, `ad-cs-attack` (AD Certificate Services) - [ ] Refresh enterprise-VPN CVE matrix quarterly to track 2026 advisories - [ ] Update architecture SVG to include the 7-skill enterprise-platform layer --- ## Sponsors

**[ApiSmart](https://www.apismart.ai/)** unifies leading LLM, image, and video models through one OpenAI-compatible API. Use one key to switch models, simplify billing, and improve reliability with automatic failover.

**[ThreatWatch360](https://threatwatch360.com)** is an AI-powered offensive-security platform: continuous Attack Surface Management, AI-assisted penetration testing, brand protection, dark-web monitoring, and Cyber Threat Intelligence in one platform. Validated findings with proof-of-concept and business-impact prioritization — signal over alert fatigue. --- ## About Operational tradecraft accumulated across bug-bounty engagements and authorized pentests, codified into Claude skills. Platform-agnostic — slot into any engagement workflow you already use, or none. **Author:** [ElementalSoul](https://github.com/elementalsouls) · GenAI Security Research **Sister project:** [Claude-OSINT](https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-OSINT) — paired skills for the recon phase that this bundle picks up after. T3 Code

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

Download · iOS · Android · Web · Docs · Discord

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any [ACP](./docs/user/providers-acp.md) agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it. ## What you get - **Your subscriptions.** T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to. - **Every agent in one place.** Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex. - **Desktop, web, and phone.** One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android. - **Remote ready.** Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or [T3 Connect](./docs/user/remote-access.md). - **Git built in.** Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button. - **Fast.** Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug. - **Open.** Source code is MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it under your own branding (see [Trademarks and forks](#trademarks-and-forks)). ## Install ### Desktop app [Download T3 Code](https://t3.codes/download) for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager: | Platform | Command | | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS | `brew install --cask t3-code` | | Windows | `winget install T3Tools.T3Code` or `scoop install extras/t3code` | | Arch Linux | `yay -S t3code-bin` | | Nix | `nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code` | | Debian, Ubuntu | `.deb` from [Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases) | ### Command line This installs the `t3` command. Run `t3` to start the server and open the web app. ```bash curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex ``` To try it once without an install, run `npx t3@latest`. ### Phone Get the app from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code). Then follow [remote access](./docs/user/remote-access.md) to connect it to your computer. ### Sign in to an agent T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`, or install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`. [Provider setup](./docs/user/install.md#providers) has the steps for each agent. [Install T3 Code](./docs/user/install.md) covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS. ## "Wait, what are you selling me?" Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar. We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork the source code and build the tool that you want, under your own name and branding. ## Documentation - [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md) - [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md) - [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md) - [Source control](./docs/user/source-control.md) - [Connect outside agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md) - [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md) [All docs](./docs/README.md) has the full list. ## Contributing We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first. - Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before you report a bug or open a pull request. - Put feature requests in [Ideas](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas). - Build from source with the [development runbook](./docs/operations/00_development.md#first-checkout). The [architecture overview](./docs/internals/01_architecture.md) explains how it works. - Get help in [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv). ## License The source code in this repository is licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE). ## Trademarks and forks The MIT license applies **only to the source code**. It does not grant any rights to T3 Tools, Inc.'s trademarks, branding, or trade dress, including the **T3 Code** name, wordmark, logos, and application icons. If you fork, redistribute, or build on T3 Code's source code: - **Use your own branding.** Replace the T3 Code name, wordmark, logos, and application icons in any public fork, redistributed build, website, package, or app store listing. - **Be explicitly clear that your project is unofficial.** Do not use the T3 Code name, wordmark, logo, or branding in your own projects without making it unmistakably clear that your project is unofficial and not affiliated with or endorsed by T3 Tools, Inc. Using our name, wordmark, logo, or branding in a way that suggests official status or affiliation is trademark infringement and unlawful. **Any project indicating or implying that it is an official version of T3 Code when it is not will be pursued to the full extent of the law.** See [TRADEMARK.md](./TRADEMARK.md) for the full trademark and branding policy.

PhoneBox

English · Türkçe · Deutsch · Français · Español · Italiano · Português · Português (Brasil) · Română · Nederlands · Polski · Русский · Ελληνικά · Tiếng Việt · 中文 (简体) · 日本語 · 한국어 · Bahasa Indonesia · ไทย · Українська · हिन्दी · Čeština · العربية · 中文（繁體）

Turn an old Android phone into a desk panel for your computer.
PC stats, AI coding sessions, music and touch controls over USB or Wi-Fi.
Windows, Linux and macOS. No root, PhoneBox account or cloud service required.

Try the live demo · Download · Quick start


Example layouts with demo data.

PhoneBox pairs a full-screen **Android app** with a small **desktop agent**. Build your panel in a browser-based visual editor: **138 widgets**, **30 templates**, multiple pages and a live preview. Connect several phones with their own layouts, or switch one phone between paired computers. ## What you can do | Use it for | What appears on the phone | |---|---| | **PC monitoring** | CPU, GPU, RAM, disks, network and ping; charts, GPU details and process controls | | **AI coding** | Claude, Codex and Antigravity quotas, reset times and burn-rate forecasts; local Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions (native and inside WSL); GitHub reviews and CI status | | **Touch controls** | App and URL shortcuts, key combinations and macros; application audio, microphone, media, OBS and system controls through [Control Deck](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md) | | **Everyday use** | Now Playing, internet radio, clocks, weather, calendars, notes, checklists, pomodoro and timers | | **Automation** | Webhook values and notifications, Home Assistant controls and rules that react to activity on the computer | Tap an AI session for its model, timing and token details. Opt in to Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode permission prompts to answer **Allow**, **Deny** (and **Always allow** for OpenCode) from the phone. Optional [CodexBar integration](docs/GUIDE.md#widgets) adds quota providers and a cost overview.


A tour with demo data: notifications, permission prompts and automatic page switching. Watch the MP4

## Quick start You need an **Android 5+ phone** (Android 6 or later recommended) and a supported computer. USB uses a data cable and USB debugging; Wi-Fi pairing works without either. Release agents include .NET, so you do not need to install the runtime. ### 1. Install the desktop agent **Windows 10/11 x64 or Windows 11 ARM64** — paste into a normal PowerShell window: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.ps1 | iex ``` **Linux or macOS** — run as your own user: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.sh | bash ``` Setup downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, offers missing dependencies and start-at-login, and opens the settings at . It can also install the Android app over USB. Run setup again to update or repair the installation while keeping settings and pairings. > **Windows signing:** release agents are still unsigned: SignPath Foundation accepted PhoneBox and test signing works, and releases are signed once its release certificate is issued. > SmartScreen or antivirus software may warn or block them. See the [code signing policy](#code-signing-policy) > and [installation warnings](docs/SETUP.md#quick-start). USB debugging should be authorized only on computers you trust. Read the scripts before running them: [Windows](setup.ps1) · [Linux/macOS](setup.sh). The [installation guide](docs/SETUP.md) covers options, dependencies, install paths, troubleshooting and uninstalling. ### 2. Connect the phone | USB | Wi-Fi only | |---|---| | Enable **Developer options → USB debugging**, connect a data cable and accept the phone's authorization prompt. Let setup install the app, or use **Settings → General → Install the phone app**. | Install the APK from the [latest release](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/releases/latest). Wi-Fi is off by default: open the settings page (tray icon, or `http://127.0.0.1:8765`), turn on **General → Wi-Fi & Tailscale → Let the phone connect without the USB cable**, click **Save**, then **Restart to apply** at the top. Choose **Pair a phone over Wi-Fi**, scan the pairing QR code and confirm the matching check code. | | Wakes and opens the panel on connection; supports app updates over adb. | No adb or developer options needed; install app updates manually unless you later configure USB. | The phone app is not in any app store; it comes only from this repository's releases. It runs on Android 5.0 and newer. An experimental iOS companion (SwiftUI, built from source with Xcode) is documented in [ios/PhoneBox](ios/PhoneBox/README.md); it has no releases and does not implement the Android-only panel features. For automatic USB/Wi-Fi fallback, enable Wi-Fi and connect the phone over USB once. [Connection details and Tailscale setup →](docs/SETUP.md#wi-fi--tailscale) ### 3. Make it yours Open (or double-click the Windows tray icon). Under **Pages**, choose a template, drag and resize widgets, then **Save**. Use **Live preview** to see unsaved edits with live data. Swipe, tap the page dots or use the phone's volume keys to move between pages.
Other installation methods - **Manual download:** unzip the agent for your system from the [release page](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/releases/latest) and run it. Install the APK on the phone. Checksums and build provenance accompany the release assets. - **Scoop (Windows):** ```powershell scoop bucket add phonebox https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox scoop install main/adb phonebox/phonebox ``` - **From source:** see the [installation guide](docs/SETUP.md#other-ways-to-install) and [development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). - **winget:** manifests are prepared in [packaging/winget](packaging/winget); see the installation guide for details.
## Pages & templates Start with Home, System, AI quotas, Sessions, Music, Planner, Automation or a Control Deck template, then adapt the 12 × 6 grid to your phone. Portrait and landscape layouts are supported. Smart Stack puts up to 12 widgets in one slot. | Home | AI sessions | |---|---| | ![Clock, weather, media and PC metrics](docs/screenshots/home.png) | ![Coding sessions and GitHub activity](docs/screenshots/work.png) | | **System** | **Layout editor** | | ![CPU, GPU, memory and network charts](docs/screenshots/system.png) | ![Pages and widget settings in the visual editor](docs/screenshots/settings-editor.png) | Screenshots use demo data. [Browse the template gallery and widgets](docs/GUIDE.md#pages--templates). Change fonts, size, spacing, corners and surfaces globally or for one page or widget with the [appearance guide](docs/APPEARANCE.md). ## Platform support | | Windows | Linux | macOS | |---|---|---|---| | Release builds | x64 | x64 / ARM64, glibc | Apple silicon / Intel | | CPU, RAM, disks, network, processes | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | GPU data | Windows counters; NVIDIA via `nvidia-smi`; extra sensors via [LibreHardwareMonitor](docs/SETUP.md#librehardwaremonitor-on-windows) | NVIDIA / AMD; Intel clock | Apple silicon, when exposed by macOS | | Media | System media sessions | `playerctl` | `nowplaying-cli`; Spotify / Music fallback | | Volume | Native | `wpctl` / `pactl` | System output; availability varies by device | | Agent interface | Tray icon + browser settings | Browser settings | Browser settings | Widgets depend on the host's hardware, installed tools and permissions. Advanced Control Deck features have [their own platform requirements](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md). Windows on ARM requires Windows 11. Musl Linux (such as Alpine) has no release build. See the [full compatibility table](docs/SETUP.md#what-works-where). ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [Installation and connections](docs/SETUP.md) | Setup options, warnings, manual and source installs, USB, Wi-Fi, Tailscale, updates, uninstall and troubleshooting | | [User guide](docs/GUIDE.md) | Template gallery, widgets, AI integrations, editor, Claude Code prompts, webhooks and automation rules | | [Appearance](docs/APPEARANCE.md) | Fonts, surfaces, presets, inheritance and live preview | | [Control Deck](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md) | Audio, media, OBS, shortcuts, tasks, protocols, dependencies and platform limits | | [Discord widget](docs/DISCORD.md) | Creating the Discord application, connecting it, controls and troubleshooting | | [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) | Architecture, local demo, builds, tests, widget sources and isolated agent runs | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Contribution scope, review expectations, privacy and required checks | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release history and unreleased changes | | [Release checklist](docs/RELEASING.md) | Maintainer build, signing and publication workflow | The [UMIDIGI BISON extras](extras/umidigi-bison) contain the reversible, no-root tune-up used on the original development phone. ## Community add-ons Add-ons are written and maintained by their authors. PhoneBox doesn't review or ship them. They run with your own rights on the computer and can change PhoneBox settings through `PUT /api/settings`, so read what an add-on does before you install it. | Add-on | What it does | What it sends outside the PC | |---|---|---| | [PhoneBox Games Tab](https://github.com/lucasaz/phonebox-games-tab) (Windows) | A Games page with live FPS, cover art and play time, through the push API and a Custom HTML widget | Store / Xbox apps' package names, with the Windows display language and region, to the Microsoft Store catalog (`displaycatalog.mp.microsoft.com`); Steam games' app IDs to the Steam store (`store.steampowered.com`), for the cover address; the phone loads cover images from Microsoft's image servers and from Steam's, whose URL contains the game's Steam app ID | | [PhoneBox for GNOME](https://github.com/Gabrielmororo180/phonebox-gnome) (Linux, GNOME) | CPU and the Claude session quota in the GNOME top bar; a click opens the panel, with page tabs, right below it. Also works as a desktop widget | Nothing of its own; the panel it opens makes the same requests as on the phone, such as the weather from `api.open-meteo.com` (see [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)) | | [Phonebox Keyboard Addon](https://github.com/Ultraalmir/Keyboard-Addon-for-PhoneBox) (Windows) | Global keyboard shortcuts for direct page navigation, plus Next / Previous controls and a tray settings panel | Nothing; it only calls the local agent on `127.0.0.1`| ## Security & privacy The desktop settings server listens on `127.0.0.1:8765`. USB reaches the agent through `adb reverse` on a loopback port of its own, over TLS pinned like Wi-Fi, with a key the phone app makes and the agent reads over adb. Optional Wi-Fi uses HTTPS on port 8766 with a pinned certificate and a paired key. Settings and pairing endpoints stay local. The phone requests configured actions by ID; commands and integration credentials stay on the computer. PhoneBox has no telemetry, analytics or accounts of its own. Optional widgets and integrations contact external services for weather, quotas, GitHub and other data, and the agent checks GitHub for updates. Supported public feeds can fall back through the agent over USB when the phone has no internet. The [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) lists outbound connections and how to disable them. Read the [security details](docs/GUIDE.md#security--privacy). To report a vulnerability, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Development The agent uses **.NET 10**; the Android app uses **Kotlin and a WebView** with plain JavaScript widgets. The optional iOS app is SwiftUI + `WKWebView` and reuses the Android panel assets; see [ios/PhoneBox/README.md](ios/PhoneBox/README.md). For Android builds, install **JDK 17** and **Android SDK Platform 35** (the SDK the app is built with; the app itself runs on Android 5.0, API 21, and later). Preview the panel and editor from source with Python 3, using simulated data: ```sh python tools/demo-server.py ``` Open or . See [development commands](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#development) for running the agent, building the APK and testing changes. Contributions are welcome; start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Code signing policy Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/). - **Windows agent:** SignPath Foundation accepted the project and a test-signed build passed; releases stay unsigned until the Foundation's release certificate is issued. The intended signing target is `PhoneBoxAgent.exe` in the `win-x64` and `win-arm64` release zips, built by the [release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml). Every signing request requires manual approval. Bundled runtime and library notices are in [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt](agent/PhoneBox.Agent/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt). - **Android app:** release APKs use the project's own signing key, independently of SignPath. - **Team roles:** committer, reviewer and signing approver: [ersinkoc](https://github.com/ersinkoc). Pull requests from other contributors are reviewed before merging. - **Privacy:** see the [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md). ## Thanks People who tested PhoneBox on their own hardware: - [anandyakshit](https://github.com/anandyakshit): Android 7 support, on an Android 7.1.1 phone ([#73](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/issues/73)). ## Sponsor

Supported by WrongStack · An open-source AI coding agent that remembers your codebase.
Explore WrongStack → · View on GitHub & give it a star ★

互不通用；携带跳数标记的请求直接拒绝（508），因此端口即使配置为本机监听的同一端口也不会自环。局域网 Key 同样由 crypto 生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于同一 0600 文件中，可在面板上单独轮换。 转发 Key 由 crypto 运行时生成、以 timingSafeEqual 比对、存放于 0600 权限文件中。它与包内用于 EAC 的共享签名材料、OAuth 客户端标识不同，后两者不能被视作仅用户持有的秘密。/ 与 /health 为存活探针，先于 Key 检查应答，但仅回答"是否在线"，获取模型清单仍需 Key。 插件的 HTTP 路由带请求信任围栏（自 v1.1 修复）：插件的 /api/our-free-model 前缀在 webServer 的最长前缀分发下优先于内核 /api，曾绕过内核鉴权。当前每个请求先经由 composition 的 connection 服务准入（与内核 /api 完全同级的 cookie/token 校验）；connection 缺失的 composition 退回结构化围栏——loopback Host、拒绝跨站 sec-fetch-site、Origin/Referer 必须与 Host 同源同端口，Host 缺失或为空也拒绝（fail closed，不回退至 socket 本地地址）。实测结果：异源 Host/Origin 返回 403，无 cookie 的回环请求返回 401。connection 为逐请求获取，因为浏览器半身要到插件加载之后才将其 provide 出来——若在 apply 时以快照方式读取一次，围栏会在整个进程周期内退化为结构化那一层（本轮将该读取改回快照后，picker-test 的 401 断言立即失败）。 公告 HTML 在客户端经严格白名单渲染：scripts/sanitize-test.mjs 使用 XSS 语料（脚本注入、事件属性、javascript:/data: URL、iframe/svg/form、样式注入、畸形标签）验证全部被丢弃；不经过任何 innerHTML sink。公告源的 feedUrl 可被用户指向任意 URL，因此渲染器按不可信输入处理。 应用内升级的完整性链（v1.3.2 加签）：清单 Ed25519 签名验证（公钥 pin 在 src/updater.js，无签名或验签失败的清单直接拒绝，未签名镜像不会被安装）→ 清单校验（semver、路径逃逸、哈希格式、base 必须为清单相对路径）→ 下载时逐文件校验 SHA-256 与字节数 → staging 回读校验 → 安装后回读校验 → 任一步失败即恢复备份；安装前强制重新拉取清单，杜绝陈旧清单。文件与代码边界见已知边界一节。 更新通道与 feedUrl 彻底解耦（v1.3.2）：feedUrl 仅重定向公告 feed，永不再重定向升级清单——此前一个设置项即可将升级源指向任意服务器并配以自配平的哈希，等同于将"修改一个设置值"升级为"在宿主进程中执行任意代码"。公告 override 本身也收紧为仅 https（回环 http 除外，本机镜像与测试仍可用）且不得内嵌凭据。目标域不受限制：任何 https 地址均可作为 feedUrl，插件按 feedPollMinutes 的间隔轮询——因此在不含 connection 服务的 composition 中（见上文鉴权说明），能够修改设置的本机调用者可让进程持续请求任意外部地址。这与插件的其余外联一样按"设置即信任"对待：能够修改 settings.json 的人本来就能安装代码。 转发监听仅绑回环地址，且按解析结果绑定（v1.3.2）：localhost 这类主机名先经 dns.lookup 解析、全部结果均为回环才放行，绑定使用解析出的 IP——当 hosts 文件或企业 DNS 将 localhost 指向可路由接口时，校验与监听不再各自为政。 卸载只需移除 bundle 条目，插件不留任何补丁；其数据目录为纯 JSON，可直接删除。 ## items.description: Does GTA VI run on PC yet? A live tracker of community recompilation and emulation efforts, updated daily.
items.readme_text:
# PortWatch VI

**Does GTA VI run on PC yet?** A static GitHub Pages site that tracks every serious community effort to recompile, emulate or port the leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI to PC. All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours.

- One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it.
- A live countdown runs to the missing executable's expected drop.
- A leaderboard card per effort shows its own bar, milestone ladder, groundwork breakdown, what works and what's blocking.
- Further sections cover the watchlist of early projects, a toolkit of asset tools, the scout's inbox of new candidates, and fake-download warnings.

No game files, keys or executables are hosted or linked, ever.

## Deploy on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new GitHub repository and push this folder to its `main` branch.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Open **Settings → Actions → General** and make sure workflows are allowed.
4. Open **Actions → Scout → Run workflow** to run the first scout. It commits fresh data and deploys the site.

Each deploy also runs `scripts/build-site.mjs`, which turns `data/tracker.json` into pages search engines can read: one page per news story (`news/<id>.html`), a news archive, an RSS feed (`news/feed.xml`) and `sitemap.xml`. It then pings [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/) (Bing, Yandex and others; no account needed) with the URLs that changed since the last deploy. For Google, add the site in Search Console and submit `sitemap.xml`.

From then on, `Scout` runs every 3 hours (00:17, 03:17, 06:17 … UTC) on GitHub's servers, so no computer of yours needs to be on. Any push to `main` redeploys the site through `Deploy site`. To change the frequency, edit the `cron` line in `.github/workflows/scout.yml`. For example, `17 6 * * *` runs it once a day. GitHub can delay scheduled runs by a few minutes when it's busy.

## What the scout does (`scripts/scout.mjs`)

1. **Refreshes** every tracked repo: stars, forks, issues, last push, commits in the last 7 days, and whether it's gone (404, or 451 for a DMCA block). It also hashes each README to notice changes.
2. **Spots claims.** If a README newly says GTA VI boots, reaches the menu or runs at some FPS, the card shows an "unverified claim" banner and the change feed records it.
3. **Discovers** new repos from GitHub and GitLab searches (`scout.queries` in `data/tracker.json`), Hacker News, Bluesky, Mastodon, Lemmy and 4chan, plus Reddit and X when keys are set, by pulling GitHub links out of posts. It also gathers **headlines** from the Google News and Bing News feeds, keeping only stories about the leak, ports, takedowns, scams or official news. And it **watches GitHub's public DMCA log** for new Take-Two or Rockstar notices, flagging any tracked project they name. On 4chan it uses the free read-only API, at one request per second. It opens only /v/ threads that mention GTA VI together with port terms (recomp, emulator, leak, executable, GitHub…), plus /vg/'s /gtag/ and /emugen/ generals. Change the boards with `scout.chan.boards`. Nothing from 4chan is shown on the site except, indirectly, repo names that pass every filter.
4. **Filters out spam** such as clone networks, download lures and "PC installer" repos. Their names are counted under *There is no download*, never linked.
5. **Filters out copies.** Re-uploads of tracked projects are flagged when they reuse a tracked project's name or have a README that is 60% or more identical, renamed copies included. Original fan games and repos without a real README are skipped too. Candidates already waiting are re-checked every run.
6. **Scores substance** from code language, size, technical depth, status tables, tests and commit activity. Repos with real code go to **New candidates**, shown as plain text and not linked until reviewed. Thin or off-topic ones are remembered and skipped.
7. **Writes news** (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Claude searches the web for takedowns, bans, confirmed leaks, legal news, scams and official announcements, then writes up to two short original articles. It runs at most every 11 hours, not on every 3-hourly scout run, to keep costs down. A source is kept only if it came up in Claude's own search. Each article's image is the source's preview image, credited and linked back; it falls back to a generated cover.
8. **Records** a change feed, the day's leader score for the sparkline, and a run summary.

### Optional secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions)

| Secret | What it enables |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **Claude review.** When a tracked README changes, or a new candidate shows up, Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) reads the README and recent commits and re-scores the effort. It also promotes or rejects candidates automatically. Guardrails clamp the output: a GTA VI milestone only counts if Claude quotes text that really appears in the repo, and groundwork can rise at most 0.3 per run. Reviews are capped at 12 per run. Each costs very roughly $0.05–0.20, depending on README size. |
| `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID` / `REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Reddit search. Reddit blocks anonymous API and RSS access, so Reddit is skipped without these. The API is free for small non-commercial use, but since late 2025 every new app needs Reddit's manual approval. Create a "script" app at reddit.com/prefs/apps, request access, and paste the client ID and secret here once approved. |
| `X_BEARER_TOKEN` | X recent search. This needs a paid X API tier. |

Without any secrets the scout still runs on every keyless source, and new finds wait in *New candidates* for review.

### Daily Claude editor (alternative to an API key)

Instead of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a scheduled Claude session on the maintainer's PC can run once a day, following [EDITOR.md](EDITOR.md). It re-scores changed projects, reviews candidates, verifies leads, keeps the countdown accurate and writes news, then commits `data/tracker.json`. It also reads 4chan's /v/, /vg/ and /g/ in full through `tools/chan-scan.ps1`, which gathers GTA VI port discussion from live threads and the public archives into a local digest (`.chan/`, never committed). The scout only picks GitHub links out of those threads. It uses the maintainer's Claude plan and needs no separate billing. It runs while the Claude desktop app is open; a missed run happens on the next launch.

## Editing the data by hand

Everything lives in `data/tracker.json`:

- `efforts[]`: each effort has a `tier` (`tracked` puts it in the race, `watchlist` lists it below). Each also carries `groundwork` (four 0–1 values), `gta` (`loads`/`boots`/`menu`/`ingame` are 0, 0.5 or 1, plus `fps` and `stability`), and short `highlights` and `blockers`.
- `exe`: drives the countdown. If the release time is announced, set `expectedAt` (ISO time) and `timeAnnounced: true`. When it drops, set `status: "released"` and `releasedAt`, and the countdown turns into a "time since release" clock.
- `candidates[]`: move one into `efforts` to promote it, or into `ignored` to dismiss it.
- `site.heroImage`: the hero photo (see below). An optional `site.heroCredit` adds a credit line under it.

Scoring is in `assets/js/scoring.js`, shared by the site and the scout. Groundwork fills 0–25%. After that, milestones sit at Exe runs 25, First frame 40, Main menu 55, In-game 70, 30 FPS 85 and Stable 100.

## Hero photo

The hero shows an original sunset illustration until the photo loads. The photo is `assets/img/hero-miami.jpg` (2400px wide): Brickell, Miami, at night, by Steele Rutherford on Unsplash, free to use under the Unsplash License without a credit line. `assets/img/social-miami.jpg` (1200×630) is the share card, made from the same photo. Give a replaced image a new filename: images are cached for 4 hours in browsers and for days by link previews. Don't use GTA VI artwork or footage there.

## Local preview

Any static server works. On Windows without Node or Python:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/serve.ps1 -Port 8080
```

Then open http://localhost:8080. To try the scout locally with Node 20+, run `node scripts/scout.mjs --dry-run`. Setting `GITHUB_TOKEN` avoids the 60-requests-per-hour anonymous limit.

## Disclaimer

Fan-made and unofficial. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games, Take-Two or Microsoft. Scores are editorial estimates from public READMEs, commits and issues, and self-reported claims are labelled. Maintainers who think their project is mis-scored can open an issue with evidence.

Join the Reverse Engineering Community
Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

--- See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project. REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion. Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine. ## Quick start **[Get started at rea.tools](https://rea.tools/get-started/)** for step-by-step instructions by operating system, agent, and analysis provider. ### Connect your agent (MCP) With [Node.js and npm](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) installed, run this from a trusted directory outside the project you plan to analyze. ```bash npx rea-agents setup ``` Choose your agent, review and approve the setup plan, then restart your agent. Setup backs up existing configuration and adds REA's MCP connection and investigation skill. See the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for supported clients, plugins, manual registration, and troubleshooting. Try asking your agent: ```text Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project. ``` Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand. ### Use REA from the terminal (CLI) Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR: ```bash npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json ``` The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as `"D:/apps/example"` on Windows. To install the `rea` command for regular use: ```bash npm install --global rea-agents rea --help ``` For native analysis, configure a provider first. The [CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) covers provider selection, native commands, snapshots, and scripting. For Linux prerequisites, see the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md#linux-owned-process-prerequisite). ### Update REA For a global npm or Bun installation, run the updater and follow its setup instructions. ```bash rea update ``` If you use `npx`, refresh your agent setup with: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` Review the setup changes and restart your agent. See [update and uninstall instructions](docs/getting-started/installation.md#diagnose-update-and-remove) for package runner options and troubleshooting. ## Showcases

DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation

Recover a position-to-pan helper from x86 instructions and verify the C reconstruction against 3,205 original-x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository

Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge

Follow the renderer’s clipboard API through preload and IPC into the main process to see how Notion handles rich clipboard data.

Read the case study

TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation

Recover fixed and aimed angle calculations from the PC-98 game’s 16-bit instructions and compare the reconstructed C++ with historical compiler output.

Read the case study · Reconstruction repository
If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your case in an [issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or a [pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls), including the target, your question, how REA helped, and what you found. ## How REA works Your agent uses REA through MCP to inspect a target and trace the relevant code. It can use the evidence REA returns to ask follow-up questions, explain behavior, or build and test an implementation. The CLI uses the same workflows. ![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg) [Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg). ## What you can analyze REA covers native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, websites, .NET assemblies, Android apps, firmware, and recorded runtime and network activity. [Supported targets and requirements](docs/reference/supported-targets.md) For native decompilation, choose a provider that supports your target format and host OS. See [choosing a deep analysis provider](docs/reference/supported-targets.md#choosing-a-deep-analysis-provider). ## Build RL environments Build a local environment from a recorded web session or a Linux desktop app so an agent can practice a task and check its result. [Build an RL environment with REA](https://rea.tools/guides/rl-environments/). ## FAQ
Which agents can use REA? Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the [supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use [manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).
Do I need a native analysis engine? Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna use your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper) for the options and their supported targets.
Do I need to start Hopper first? REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open Hopper manually if needed. See [Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).
What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup` to register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart your agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).
What code does REA return? Native analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis recovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to write and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.
Does REA upload my app? REA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its model provider has its own data policy.
What should I do if I hit a bug? Update first; a recent release may already fix it. For a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`: ```bash rea update ``` For agent setup through `npx`: ```bash npx rea-agents@latest setup ``` If you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart it. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) with your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.
## Documentation Start with the website's [worked guides](https://rea.tools/guides/). For exact options, prerequisites and result contracts: - [Installation and setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md): agent registration, provider configuration, updates and uninstall. - [Readiness and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#check-readiness-for-your-task): diagnose one agent or analysis engine. - [CLI and Evidence](docs/getting-started/cli.md): commands, provider selection, snapshots, import/export and exit statuses. - [MCP contracts](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md) and [agent prompts](docs/getting-started/mcp-prompts.md): tool results, sessions and guided investigations. - [Tool catalog](docs/reference/mcp-contracts.md#generated-catalog): generated inventory of tools, providers and CLI commands. Report vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Community & Support - **Discord** — Ask questions and share what you’re investigating with our passionate community of over 50,000 reverse engineers and builders! [![Join the REA Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join%20Discord-5865F2?style=flat-square&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) - **Twitter / X** — Follow [@reatools](https://x.com/reatools) for updates and announcements. - **Feedback & Ideas** — Want a new feature or support for a file format? [Open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) or [join our Discord](https://discord.gg/GkcryMnJDM) and let us know. ## Star history 🎉 **400,000 GitHub stars — thank you!** Thanks to everyone using REA, reporting bugs, requesting features, testing builds, and contributing fixes. ## Contributing We'd love your help with REA! [Open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues) to report a bug or suggest a feature, or [send a pull request](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pulls) to improve the code or docs. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and checks. See the [testing guide](docs/development/testing.md) for verification lanes. ## Disclaimer See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md) for responsible-use guidance. The project's position on illegal or unauthorized use covers all REA versions, distribution channels, and platforms; each copy retains its applicable licenses. REA is for lawful research, education, interoperability, software preservation, and analysis of software you own or are authorized to examine. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) REA-authored code is licensed under MIT. Third-party material retains its own licenses and copyright notices; see [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the dependency inventory, preserved license texts, and external-tool terms. **You must legally obtain and be authorized to use commercial tools**, including IDA Pro / Hex-Rays decompilers, Hopper, and JEB, under their applicable licenses. REA grants no tool license, key, or activation entitlement. Trials and demos remain subject to vendor terms, including user, feature, automation, and output sharing restrictions. Cracked copies, stolen keys, unauthorized key sharing, and bypassing license restrictions are not authorized. This guidance does not amend MIT or third-party licenses.
